title: Signal origins and dashboard tile taxonomy
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a planning/working sketch that maps where operational signals originate (service, model, infra, client), and proposes a compact taxonomy for dashboard tiles used by oncall, product, and platform engineers. Goal: make it unambiguous which metric belongs to which tile, how traces should anchor tiles, and what sampling/refresh constraints apply so dashboards stay useful without exploding query cost.

Audience and context:
- Primary: operator/observability engineers building or maintaining inference dashboards.
- Secondary: SREs, Serving Runtime, Product owners for model rollouts.
- Assumption: we want the same tile taxonomy to be usable across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private contexts; per-tenant filters are allowed but tile semantics should not change.

High-level principles (short):
1) Single responsibility tiles: each tile answers one operational question (e.g., "Are token latencies degrading for 1P models?").
2) Signal provenance first: label each metric/span with a single origin (service|model-sidecar|gpu-node|client-proxy).
3) Trace anchor: every tile must list a canonical trace/span link that is the primary debugging handoff.
4) Cost budget: tiles categorized by query cost tier (cheap|moderate|expensive). Prefer pre-aggregates for cheap/moderate tiles.
5) Sampling and TTL: define sampling rate and retention for debug traces per tile.

Signal origins taxonomy (recommended labels):
- service_runtime: control plane, routing, request queuing, request sizing (examples: route_select_ms, preflight_latency_ms).
- model_executor: model forward/backward path inside the serving runtime (examples: token_emit_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate).
- gpu_infra: GPU scheduling, load, memory pressure, ECC events (examples: gpu_util_pct, gpu_memory_bytes_free).
- network_edge: client-facing network (LB latency, TLS handshake failures).
- client_app: client-side latency and tokenization issues (tokenized_len_distribution).
- cost_meter: billing/chargeback signals (tokens_generated_count, embedding_units).

For each origin the recommended instrumenting keys and annotation conventions:
- metric_name: dot-delimited, lower_snake, root by origin, e.g., service_runtime.request_queue_ms.p50
- trace_annotation: add tags "origin=<origin>", "model_family=<name>", "route_id=<id>", "tenant_id=<id>"
- span_name convention: origin.short_action e.g., model_executor.forward, service_runtime.enqueue

Dashboard tile taxonomy (compact):
- Tile A: Live health strip (cheap)
  - Purpose: one-line glance for operator (OK / degraded / critical)
  - Signals: overall request_rate, error_rate_1m, tail_latency_p99 (pre-aggregated)
  - Origins: aggregated across service_runtime + model_executor
  - Query cadence / TTL: 15s refresh, 1h data retention on hot panels
  - Trace anchor: last_error_trace_id (sampled 100% for errors, see sampling below)
- Tile B: Latency heatband (moderate)
  - Purpose: breakdown of latency by stage (enqueue, forward, emit)
  - Signals: latency_p{50,90,95,99} per stage, kv_cache_hit_rate by stage
  - Origins: service_runtime, model_executor
  - Cadence: 30s, retention 7d for aggregates, 30d for p90
  - Trace anchor: span matching slow_stage with highest contribution to p99

- Tile C: Cold cache & model warm metrics (moderate/expensive)
  - Purpose: show prefix-warmth, kv_cache_evictions, cold-start counts
  - Signals: kv_warm_pct_by_route, cold_start_count_1h, model_load_time_ms
  - Origins: model_executor, gpu_infra
  - Cadence: 1m, retention 30d for trend analysis
  - Trace anchor: earliest span with model.load or kv_fetch

- Tile D: Tenant cost micro-dashboard (cheap)
  - Purpose: cost signal for tenant-weighted views
  - Signals: token_units_by_tenant (1h rollup), anomalous_spend_flag
  - Origins: cost_meter + service_runtime
  - Cadence: 5m (rollups), retention 90d

- Tile E: Error taxonomy explorer (expensive)
  - Purpose: drill-down on top error classes across layers
  - Signals: top_error_types, error_rate_by_origin, exception_trace_samples
  - Origins: all
  - Cadence: on-demand (expensive queries) with cached 1h snapshot

Sampling strategy (practical):
- Default trace capture: 0.1% of successful requests, 100% of error requests (error = any 5xx or model exception) for 30d.
- Error sampling is critical for tile A/E handoffs; ensure last_error_trace_id is stored in a cheap DB index to avoid heavy queries.
- Conditional size sampling: for latency > p95, upsample to 5% for next 10 minutes to capture tails during incidents.
- Tenant-aware sampling: for tenants flagged as high-cost or on Dedicated, increase baseline to 1%.

Metric definitions (compact canonical set, to be added to metric-contract registry):
- request_rate: origin=service_runtime, type=gauge, unit=req/s, aggregation=sum per 1m
- error_rate_1m: origin=service_runtime, type=ratio, numerator=errors, denominator=requests, window=1m
- token_emit_ms.p90: origin=model_executor, type=histogram, unit=ms, quantiles=[50,90,95,99]
- kv_cache_hit_rate: origin=model_executor, type=ratio, note=label by route_id and model_version
- gpu_util_pct: origin=gpu_infra, type=gauge, unit=percent, aggregation=avg over 10s
- cold_start_count_1h: origin=model_executor, type=count, window=1h, label=model_variant

Trace annotations and span design (examples and recommended tags):
- Root span: service_runtime.request (tags: tenant_id, route_id, model_family, request_id)
- model_executor.forward span: (tags: batch_size, seq_len, quantization_profile)
- kv_fetch span: (tags: kv_key_count, kv_hit=true/false)
- network_edge.tls span: (tags: client_ip_hash, tls_version, lb_id)
- Attach metrics to spans using standardized keys: metric.request_latency_ms, metric.kv_misses

Dashboard operational notes (practical recommendations):
- Each tile must document: What question does it answer? Who owns it? Cost tier. Trace anchor. Where the metric contract lives (confluence id).
- Use per-tile badges for "cost tier" and "trace-ready": a small UI indicator that the tile is trace-anchored and which trace tags are available.
- Panel templates: create JSON templates for each tile type (A..E) with parameterized variables (tenant_id, model_family) in repo github.com/redwood-inference/obs-dashboards/templates.
- Alert knobs: only allow alerts on cheap/moderate tiles and route to escalation playbooks. Avoid firing alerts from expensive ad-hoc explorer tiles.

Ownership and onboarding checklist (short):
- Owner assigns metric steward for each new metric and records contract link.
- Create tile from template, verify trace anchor populates for sample requests.
- Run cost simulation for 30d (estimated query QPS) before enabling expensive tiles in team dashboards.
- Add tile to dashboard index (README) and mark owner + last verification date.

Open questions and follow-ups (work items):
- Should we add a dedicated low-latency CDN metric origin for edge-cached model shards? (Shall open DISCUSS-EDGE ticket)
- Decide retention policy for p99 histograms beyond 30d (tradeoff: trend vs cost).
- Implement a cheap last_error_trace_id index in our trace store; prototype ticket JIRA-OPS-1042.

Quicklinks / references:
- Confluence: Observability metric contracts (CONFLUENCE-OBS-42)
- GitHub templates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-dashboards/tree/main/templates
- Existing related doc references: JIRA-OPS-987 (kv-prefetch experiments)

Notes to self / sketch ideas (informal):
- Could try a "tile health color" derived from fractional contribution to error budget (makes cross-tenant triage faster).
- Consider small histogram micro-tiles for embedding latencies binned by seq len, cheap if we pre-aggregate with quantile sketches.
- When during a rollout, toggle tile mode to high-sensitivity (increases trace sampling for that route for 1h).

If you're reviewing: focus feedback on the tile taxonomy, sampling numbers (are they too aggressive?), and trace anchor UX ideas.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-10: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-02-18: added sampling guidance and tile cost tiers (Ethan)
- 2025-03-01: clarified metric names and trace annotation conventions (Lena)
